chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who gives a bribe to another man so that he will move from his house and the briber will live in it. He said, 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.رِشْوَة: Bribe or gift given to influence action
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm in it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: Is giving a bribe to move someone out of a house permissible in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rules that paying a sum to induce a tenant or owner to vacate a property is permissible (*la ba'sa bihi*), distinguishing it from corrupt bribery (*risha*) given for unjust advantage. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic view that such payments are essentially a voluntary transaction or compensation for loss of residence, provided there is no deceit or coercion involved. It underscores the flexibility in commercial dealings (*mu'amalat*) where mutual consent validates the transfer of possession.
